claims.claim: For d=δ⁺(D)≥1, a directed cycle of length at least d+1 can be found in polynomial time; additionally, n<d+k is an immediate sound NO condition. Thus the target is completely solved for k=1.
claims.evidence: Let P=v₁…v_p be a maximal simple directed path. Every out-neighbor of v_p is then among v₁,…,v_{p−1}. If v_i is its earliest out-neighbor, all at least d distinct out-neighbors lie among the p−i vertices v_i,…,v_{p−1}; hence p−i≥d. The closing cycle v_i…v_pv_i has p−i+1≥d+1 vertices. Greedy extension takes at most n−1 extensions and is polynomial. Since every cycle has at most n vertices, n<d+k is a sound NO test. For k=1 the construction always supplies the requested d+1 cycle.
claims.witness: The constructive witness is v_i→v_{i+1}→…→v_p→v_i from any greedily obtained maximal path, with i the earliest out-neighbor of v_p.
claims.search_method: Independent deductive proof plus exhaustive exact testing of every loopless digraph on 2–4 vertices; all 9,687 deterministic maximal-path runs with positive minimum outdegree returned a cycle of length at least d+1, and 11,015 applicable size-based NO conditions were checked.

claims.claim: For any integer L≥2, existence of a directed cycle of length at least L is exactly equivalent to a short-leg two-way linkage, yielding an explicit O(n^L(n+m)) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: For an enumerated simple L-vertex directed path P=v₁…v_L, a simple v_L-to-v₁ path after deleting v₂,…,v_{L−1} intersects P only at its endpoints, so its union with P is a simple directed cycle of length at least L. Conversely, any cycle of length at least L supplies P as L consecutive vertices and supplies the required return path as the complementary cycle segment. There are O(n^L) ordered tuples, and adjacency checking plus one reachability search costs O(n+m) for nontrivial L≤n; L>n is immediately false. Thus the stated equivalence and runtime follow.
claims.witness: Each feasible tuple and return path form a cycle; in the reverse direction, any qualifying cycle yields a tuple of L consecutive vertices and its complementary return segment.
claims.search_method: Independent proof in both directions and exact comparison of the linkage predicate with exact subset-DP circumference for 16,584 graph/threshold cases over all loopless digraphs on 2–4 vertices, including L=n+1.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially checkable upper-bound certificate: if X is an independent vertex set and every arc entering X from outside X has its tail in S⊆V(D)\X, then every directed cycle has length at most n−|X|+|S|.
claims.evidence: For every x∈C∩X, independence forces its predecessor on C to lie outside X, and the entering-arc hypothesis then places that predecessor in C∩S. Different x have different predecessors because each cycle vertex has only one successor on C. This is an injection C∩X→C∩S, so |C∩X|≤|S|. At most n−|X| vertices of C lie outside X, giving |C|≤n−|X|+|S|. Independence, set containment, and the entering-arc condition are all checkable by scanning vertices and arcs.
claims.witness: The certificate’s witness map sends each x∈C∩X to its distinct predecessor in C∩S.
claims.search_method: Independent injection proof plus exhaustive exact validation of all 131,755 valid (D,X,S) certificates arising from every loopless digraph on 2–4 vertices and every eligible pair of subsets.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥4 there are 2-strong NO-instances with arbitrarily large minimum outdegree and with n≥d+k; indeed their circumference is exactly d+3.
claims.evidence: Take arbitrary q≥3, a≥k−1, a q-vertex complete bidirected core Q containing x,y, and an a-set A. Add all A→Q arcs and all {x,y}→A arcs, with no others. After any one vertex is deleted, the surviving core is strong, every surviving A-vertex reaches it, and at least one of x,y reaches every surviving A-vertex; hence the digraph is 2-strong. Its minimum outdegree is d=q−1. Each A-vertex on a cycle must have predecessor x or y, so a simple cycle uses at most two A-vertices and has length at most q+2. For distinct a₁,a₂∈A and an ordering z₁,…,z_{q−2} of Q\{x,y}, the cycle x,a₁,z₁,…,z_{q−2},y,a₂,x has length q+2=d+3. Since a≥k−1 gives n=q+a≥q−1+k=d+k, while k≥4 gives d+3<d+k, these are NO-instances. Letting q grow makes d unbounded.
claims.witness: The parameterized family above, with arbitrary q≥3 and a≥k−1, witnesses the assertion; the displayed q+2-vertex cycle witnesses exact circumference.
claims.search_method: Independent symbolic verification of degrees, 2-strongness, upper bound, matching cycle, and parameter inequalities; supplemented by exact checks for 20 pairs 3≤q≤6, 2≤a≤6, all 170 single-vertex deletions, and 40 applicable k-values.

claims.claim: The target has a polynomial-time solution on semicomplete digraphs: such an input is YES exactly when n≥d+k, and a Hamiltonian directed cycle can be constructed when YES.
claims.evidence: A 2-strong input is strong. Begin with a directed cycle C in a strong semicomplete digraph. Insert any outside z for which c_i→z→c_{i+1}. If no such insertion exists, semicompleteness and propagation around C imply that each outside vertex either is strictly dominated by all of C or strictly dominates all of C. Strongness forces both classes to be nonempty and, on a path from the dominated class to C, forces an arc u→v from a C-dominated vertex u to a C-dominating vertex v. Then any edge c_i→c_{i+1} can be replaced by c_i→u→v→c_{i+1}. Each iteration adds one or two vertices, so exhaustive scans give a polynomial construction of a Hamiltonian cycle. Consequently a cycle of length at least d+k exists exactly when the necessary size condition n≥d+k holds.
claims.witness: The constructive witness is the Hamiltonian cycle obtained by repeated one-vertex insertion c_i→z→c_{i+1} or two-vertex insertion c_i→u→v→c_{i+1}.
claims.search_method: Independent proof of the no-insertion dichotomy and strongness transition, plus an exact implementation tested on all 59,808 semicomplete digraphs on 2–5 vertices. It constructed Hamiltonian cycles in all 52,528 strong instances and checked the threshold equivalence on all 19,777 2-strong instances.

target_evidence: The exact target requests an f(k)n^{O(1)} algorithm for all 2-strong digraphs. The draft does not establish that target: Claim 0 handles only k=1; Claim 1 has exponent L=d+k and therefore is not FPT in k; Claim 2 supplies only certificates when suitable sets are available; Claim 3 is an obstruction family rather than a general decision algorithm; and Claim 4 handles only the semicomplete subclass. These are correct and material partial advances, especially the explicit 2-strong obstruction and the complete restricted-class algorithm, but they do not resolve the general target. The claimed resolution is PARTIAL, and the final writeup explicitly says that the required FPT algorithm was not obtained, so that resolution is accurate and not overclaimed.
